metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe-index get <data-dir> <group> <name> --json` (PROP-008 §2.2): one package's usable versions by its `(group, name)` identity, with the versions this build refused named beside them. Read by scripts and agents (PROP-044 §6.5 — a CLI `--json` report is a format plain text; `foreign_parsers = many`). Source of truth for the writer: `crates/vibe-index/src/cli/get.rs` (`GetEnvelope`); the generated reader this schema owns lives in `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index_cli/e1/get_report/`.

Whether the asked-for fact came back: `true` for a whole-package ask whenever the `(group, name)` identity stands in the index — even when every version is refused — and for a `--version` ask exactly when that version was served. `false` names an identity (or version) the index does not hold or cannot act on; `unavailable` says why.
The reverse-FQDN group qualifier of the ask, echoed back verbatim.
The bare package name of the ask, echoed back verbatim.

Every version of the package this build can act on (`usable_versions`, PROP-044 §4.5), narrowed to the ask when `--version` named one. Required member: a not-found ask writes `[]`, never an absent key — the writer has no `skip_serializing_if` here.

Versions of this package this build refused to serve — named, not hidden (PROP-044 §4.5), narrowed to the ask when `--version` named one. Absent when there are none (the writer carries `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`).

One version this build refused to serve, and why — the row every `vibe-index` answering surface carries (`crates/vibe-index/src/index/quarantine.rs`, `Unavailable`). It names the full coordinate even inside an envelope that already names the package: a row that identifies itself survives being copied out of its envelope by a script. Local to this schema family: `formats/vocabularies.json` does not (yet) carry it, and each of the six report schemas that need it declare their own copy.
The refused version's bare package name.

The reader capabilities of `must_understand` this build lacks, in the record's own order. Required member: a refusal always writes its list, `[]` never occurring in practice today (a row exists exactly because the list is non-empty) but lawful on the wire — the writer has no skip here.
What a person or a script does about it — the fixed two-part text `recipe_for` builds (the explanation with the PROP-044 anchor, then the `fix:` surface).
